metadata.suite_name: SmartHire Knowledge Graph Pipeline SHAP Validation

baseline_provenance.provenance: Observed empirical pass rates over authentic Kaggle resume cohort

methodological_declarations.algebraic_additivity_vs_faithfulness: Algebraic additivity (sum(phi_i) == Score - E[Score]) is an exact mathematical property of the closed-form Shapley game over linearly separable requirements, not an empirical proof of explanation faithfulness. Faithfulness is independently validated via AOPC feature-perturbation decay.
methodological_declarations.predictive_validity_limitation: Predictive validity against real-world human job performance is uncompleted because open-source resume corpora lack human post-hire ratings or validated competence ground truth.
methodological_declarations.llm_explainability_boundary: SHAP attributions explain the deterministic candidate-matching score (Graph_ATS). Unstructured text generated by multi-agent LLM prompts is probabilistic and is not explained by SHAP.
methodological_declarations.aopc_non_monotone_caveat: In redundant-satisfier profiles (multiple skills covering the same requirement), comprehensiveness decay is non-monotone: removing the top-SHAP skill may not immediately reduce the score because another skill redundantly covers that requirement. This is structurally correct behaviour for the set-coverage game, not an explainability failure.

perturbation_faithfulness_all.note: All-N includes degenerate profiles; use eligible-N stats for research reporting.

perturbation_faithfulness_eligible.scientific_interpretation: Among eligible profiles (>=2 extracted skills), comprehensiveness decay exceeds sufficiency decay, confirming that top-SHAP features drive score reductions more than null-player tokens. Non-monotone decay observed in redundant-satisfier profiles is documented and expected for this set-coverage game structure.

algebraic_reconstruction_check.description: The following are algebraic reconstruction-error checks, not predictive-validity statistics. Since reconstructed_score = E[Score] + sum(phi_j) = E[Score] + (Score - E[Score]) = Score, the max reconstruction error is guaranteed to be zero by construction.
algebraic_reconstruction_check.note: Reconstruction error == 0 is an algebraic certainty, not an empirical result. Spearman rho and R² between raw and reconstructed scores are trivially 1.0 by construction and are NOT reported as empirical validation statistics.
